**Alcohol:** A drug found in drinks such as beer, waragi, wine and spirits, which slows down the working of the brain and body.

**Alcoholic:** A person who is addicted to alcohol.

Effects of smoking

Definitions
**Drug:** Any substance that changes the way the body or mind works.

blocks.x: **Sanitation:** Keeping the surroundings clean and disposing of human waste and rubbish safely so that people stay healthy.
**Poor sanitation causes:** cholera, typhoid, dysentery, diarrhoea, worms, bilharzia, hepatitis, jiggers, and flies and bad smells everywhere.
(a) The ordinary (conventional) pit latrine
A pit dug in the ground with a **slab** and a **squat hole** with a cover, walls and a roof.

**Advantages:** cheap and easy to build with local materials; needs no water. **Disadvantages:** smells; attracts flies; fills up and must be replaced; can pollute wells if too close or too shallow; may collapse in sandy soil or when flooded.
(b) The VIP latrine
**VIP** stands for **Ventilated Improved Pit** latrine.

**Its special parts:** a **vent pipe** running from the pit up above the roof, covered at the top with a **fly screen**; a **dark interior**; and a squat hole that is **left uncovered** so air can flow.

**How it works:** the sun heats the vent pipe, air rises up it and pulls the smell out of the pit, while fresh air comes in through the door. **Flies** in the dark pit fly towards the light at the top of the pipe and are trapped by the **screen**.
**Advantages:** almost **no smell**; controls flies; more comfortable to use. **Disadvantage:** costs more to build than an ordinary latrine.
(c) The Ecosan toilet
**Ecosan** means **ecological sanitation** — a toilet that turns human waste into manure.

Urine and faeces are **separated**: urine goes into a container through a separate opening, and faeces fall into a sealed vault where **ash or dry soil** is added after every use. When one vault is full it is closed and the second is used; after several months the dried material is safe to use as **manure**.

**Advantages:** no pit to dig deep, so it suits **rocky, sandy, waterlogged or crowded** areas; provides manure; does not pollute the ground water; no smell if ash is used. **Disadvantages:** costs more; needs careful use and training; ash must always be available; some people dislike handling the material.
(d) The potty

A small **portable container** used by babies and small children who cannot use the latrine. It must be **emptied into the latrine at once** and washed with clean water and soap, then dried in the sun. Never empty it in the compound or the bathroom.
(e) The water closet (flush toilet)
A toilet with a **cistern, a bowl with a water seal, and a handle or button** that flushes the waste with water into a **septic tank or sewer line**.

**Advantages:** clean, no smell, comfortable, indoors, no flies. **Disadvantages:** needs **plenty of piped water**; expensive to build and maintain; blocks easily if wrong things are thrown in; useless where there is no water supply.

sections.title: 3. IMPORTANCE OF USING A TOILET OR LATRINE

items: It stops the spread of diseases such as **cholera, typhoid, dysentery, diarrhoea and worms**.
It keeps the compound, gardens and water sources **free from human waste**.
It controls **flies and bad smells**.
It protects **water sources** from contamination.
It gives **privacy and dignity**.
It keeps the home **clean and pleasant** and free from shame.
It is required by **public health law**; every home should have a latrine.

blocks.x: **Remember the disease path:** faeces → **flies, fingers, food, fluids and fields** → mouth. Using a latrine and washing hands **breaks that path**.
Proper use

Use the latrine **every time** — never the bush or the compound · **aim into the hole** and keep the slab clean · **cover the hole** after use in an ordinary latrine (but a VIP hole is left open) · put used paper in the pit, not on the floor · **add ash** after each use in an Ecosan toilet · **flush** the water closet after use · **wash your hands with soap and clean water** afterwards · teach small children to use the potty and empty it into the latrine.
Maintenance

**Sweep and scrub** the floor and slab daily · pour water or disinfectant where needed · keep a **hand-washing facility with soap** at the door · repair a cracked slab, a broken door or a leaking roof at once · keep the **vent pipe screen** in good order on a VIP · keep the door closed so animals do not enter · **do not throw rubbish, sanitary pads, polythene or stones into the pit** — they fill it up and block flush toilets · plant grass or trees around it to reduce dust · when the pit is about **half a metre from full**, close it and dig a new one.
Where to site a latrine

At least **30 metres from a water source** and **downhill** from it · at least 6 metres from the house, downwind · on firm, well-drained ground · away from where children play · with a clear path so people can use it at night.

Care of a pregnant mother (antenatal care)

Attend the **antenatal clinic** early and regularly · eat a **balanced diet** with plenty of iron and vitamins · take the medicines and supplements given · sleep under a **treated mosquito net** · rest enough and avoid heavy work · avoid **alcohol, smoking and self-medication** · keep clean · plan to deliver at a **health centre with a trained health worker**.
Problems in pregnancy

Anaemia · malaria · high blood pressure · miscarriage · bleeding · swollen legs and hands · vomiting too much · obstructed labour · malnutrition · infections including HIV. Any of these needs a **health worker at once**.
Teenage pregnancy
**Teenage pregnancy** is pregnancy in a girl below 20 years, whose body is not yet ready.

**Effects:** danger to the health and life of the girl and the baby · obstructed labour and fistula · low birth weight · dropping out of school · loss of future opportunities · poverty · rejection and stigma · unsafe abortion, which can kill.

**Prevention:** stay in school · **abstain from sex** · avoid bad company, alcohol and drugs · avoid gifts and lifts from older people (sugar daddies and sugar mummies) · know your rights and report abuse to a trusted adult · get correct information from parents, teachers and health workers.
*Defilement — a sexual act with a person below 18 — is a serious crime in Uganda, and any child who is abused should tell a trusted adult and report it immediately. It is never the child's fault.*

**Family planning:** Deciding **how many children to have and when to have them**, and using acceptable methods to achieve this.
**Child spacing** means leaving enough time — usually at least **two to three years** — between one birth and the next.

items: Protects the **mother's health**, giving her body time to recover.
Gives each child better **care, food, health and education**.
Reduces **infant and maternal deaths**.
Helps the family **plan its money** and avoid poverty.
Reduces very rapid **population growth** and the pressure on land and services.
Allows parents to work, study and rest.

**Growth** is an increase in the size and weight of the body, while **development** is the change that makes the body able to do more, such as walking, talking and reproducing.
Puberty is the stage at which the reproductive organs become mature and a young person becomes able to produce children. It begins at about **10–14 years in girls** and **12–16 years in boys**.
Adolescence is the period of change between childhood and adulthood, affecting the body, the mind and the feelings.

**Girls:** breasts develop; hips widen; menstruation begins; pubic and armpit hair grows (also oily skin, rapid growth). **Boys:** the voice deepens; the chest and shoulders broaden; wet dreams begin; facial, pubic and armpit hair grows.
Any four of: wanting independence; strong peer influence; quick changes of mood; shyness; interest in the opposite sex; wanting privacy; new interest in appearance.

**Primary** characteristics are the reproductive organs present at **birth**, for example the testes and the ovaries. **Secondary** characteristics appear at **puberty**, for example breasts in girls and a deep voice in boys.

Any four: **testes** — produce sperm cells; **scrotum** — holds the testes and keeps them cool; **sperm duct** — carries sperms; **urethra** — passes semen and urine out; **penis** — the organ through which semen and urine leave the body.

Any four: **ovaries** — produce egg cells; **fallopian tubes** — carry the egg and are where fertilisation happens; **uterus** — where the baby develops; **cervix** — the neck of the uterus; **vagina** — the passage to the outside.
Sperm cells are produced in the **testes**; egg cells are produced in the **ovaries**.
Menstruation is the monthly flow of blood and the lining of the uterus through the vagina when the egg has not been fertilised. The cycle is about **28 days**.
Fertilisation is the joining of a **sperm cell and an egg cell**. It takes place in the **fallopian tube (oviduct)**.

**Conception** — the fertilised egg attaching to the wall of the uterus and beginning to grow; **zygote** — the single cell formed at fertilisation; **gestation** — the period the baby develops in the womb.
Pregnancy lasts about **nine months (40 weeks)**. The **placenta** supplies the baby with food and oxygen from the mother and carries away its waste.
Any four of: the monthly periods stop; morning sickness; the breasts enlarge; the abdomen grows; tiredness; changes in appetite.

Any six of: attend antenatal clinic early and regularly; eat a balanced diet rich in iron; take the supplements given; sleep under a treated mosquito net; rest and avoid heavy work; avoid alcohol, smoking and self-medication; keep clean; deliver at a health centre with a trained health worker.
Any four of: anaemia, malaria, high blood pressure, miscarriage, bleeding, excessive vomiting, obstructed labour, malnutrition, infections including HIV.

**Effects (any five):** danger to the health and life of the girl and baby; obstructed labour and fistula; low birth weight; dropping out of school; poverty; stigma and rejection; unsafe abortion. **Prevention (any four):** stay in school; abstain from sex; avoid bad company, alcohol and drugs; refuse gifts and lifts from older people; report abuse to a trusted adult; get correct information from parents and health workers.

Any six of: bathe daily and wash the private parts with clean water; wear clean cotton underwear and change it daily; wipe from front to back; use and change clean sanitary materials; never insert anything into the private parts; avoid harmful traditional practices; treat itching or discharge early; abstain from sex; report anybody who touches you wrongly.

Family planning is deciding how many children to have and when to have them, using acceptable methods. **Importance (any five):** it protects the mother's health; it gives each child better care and education; it reduces infant and maternal deaths; it helps the family plan its money; it slows very rapid population growth; it allows parents to work and rest.

**Natural:** abstinence, the calendar (rhythm) method, breastfeeding in the early months. **Artificial:** condoms, pills, injections (also implants, the loop). **Myths corrected:** "family planning makes a woman permanently barren" — most methods are **reversible** and fertility returns when they are stopped; "it is only for women" — it is the responsibility of **both** partners.
